task.title: Tempo payment method (8 sub-tasks 13a-h)
task.body:
On-chain TIP-20 transfer verification via Tempo's JSON-RPC. Implements MPP.Methods.Tempo supporting both `type="hash"` (client-broadcast) and `type="transaction"` (server-broadcast) credential paths.

Shipped:
- TransferWithMemo support — memo matching for `transferWithMemo(address,uint256,bytes32)` calls, enforced per spec when `methodDetails.memo` is configured. Discovered via real Moderato receipts that the `memo` parameter is `indexed` (topic, not data field).
- Fee payer co-signing — server-side fee sponsorship for `feePayer: true` with 0x78 domain signing and call scope validation (whitelist of 4 allowed selector patterns matching mppx `callScopes`).
- Optimistic broadcast mode — `wait_for_confirmation: false` simulates payment call via `eth_call` then broadcasts asynchronously, returning an optimistic receipt without waiting for block inclusion.
- Transaction dedup store (MPP.Tempo.Store behaviour) — pluggable replay protection with get/1, put/2, and optional atomic check_and_mark/2 callbacks; different dedup semantics per credential path (hash: post-verification mark; transaction: pre-broadcast reservation).
- Built-in ConCacheStore (MPP.Tempo.ConCacheStore) — ETS-based dedup store with automatic TTL via ConCache.
- v-value normalization in recover_sender/2 (legacy 27/28 → recid 0/1) for ox/tempo SDK interop.
- ox/tempo cross-validation of 0x76 RLP encoding via QuickBEAM + esbuild bundle against the ox/tempo TypeScript SDK.
task.implemented: Shipped MPP.Methods.Tempo for on-chain TIP-20 transfer verification over Tempo's JSON-RPC, supporting both client-broadcast (type=hash) and server-broadcast (type=transaction) credential paths — including TransferWithMemo matching (indexed memo topic), fee-payer co-signing with 0x78 domain signing and call-scope validation, optimistic broadcast mode, a pluggable dedup store behaviour with a built-in ConCacheStore, v-value normalization in recover_sender/2, and ox/tempo cross-validation of 0x76 RLP encoding.

task.title: Generic EVM method
task.body:
On-chain payment verification for any EVM chain (Ethereum, Base, Polygon, Arbitrum, etc.). `MPP.Methods.EVM` implements the `MPP.Method` behaviour.

- Hash-only credential path: client broadcasts tx, sends hash, server verifies receipt.
- ERC-20 transfers verified via Transfer event log parsing (`Onchain.Transfer.parse_logs/1`).
- Native ETH transfers verified via transaction value + recipient matching.
- Currency convention: ERC-20 tokens use contract address; native ETH uses "ETH" or zero address.
- Sepolia integration tests added: ERC-20 via WETH (wraps ETH → deposit() → transfer), native ETH, error cases, full 402 flow.

Hash-only verification (no signed-tx broadcast path) — simpler, universally works across all EVM chains without chain-specific transaction types. RPC calls via Req directly (Onchain.RPC uses Signet → Finch and bypasses Req entirely; Req enables Req.Test stubbing).
task.implemented: Shipped MPP.Methods.EVM implementing on-chain payment verification for any EVM chain via a hash-only credential path — ERC-20 transfers verified through Transfer event log parsing and native ETH via transaction value/recipient matching, with RPC calls over Req (for Req.Test stubbing) and Sepolia integration tests covering ERC-20 (WETH), native ETH, error cases, and the full 402 flow.

task.title: Amount and decimals helpers
task.body:
`MPP.Amount` — pure integer/string arithmetic for converting human-readable amounts to base units.

- `parse_units/2` — "1.5" + 6 decimals → "1500000" (cross-validated against mpp-rs test vectors)
- `with_base_units/2` — applies parse_units to any intent struct's amount field
- `parse_dollar_amount/2` — "$1.50" + decimals → `{"150", "usd", 2}` with currency symbol detection ($, €, £, ¥) and suffix codes ("1.50 USD")

Caller supplies decimals explicitly (no currency-to-decimals inference) — matches mppx and mpp-rs design. Zero allowed (zero-amount charges valid for identity/proof flows). No floating point anywhere — all arithmetic via string splitting and padding.

BREAKING in v0.4.0: `parse_dollar_amount/1` → `parse_dollar_amount/2` (caller supplies decimals explicitly). Implicit inference created correctness risks (HUF/TWD classification is debatable) and diverged from spec's "explicit configuration" philosophy.
task.implemented: Shipped MPP.Amount for pure integer/string base-unit conversion with no floating point — parse_units/2 (cross-validated against mpp-rs vectors), with_base_units/2 over intent structs, and parse_dollar_amount/2 with currency-symbol/suffix detection; caller supplies decimals explicitly (BREAKING in v0.4.0: parse_dollar_amount/1 → /2).

task.title: Verifier extraction + JCS
task.body:
Extracted the verification pipeline from `MPP.Plug` into a transport-neutral `MPP.Verifier` module. Added `MPP.JCS` for RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme.

- `MPP.JCS` — RFC 8785 canonical JSON (MPP subset: ASCII keys, string/integer/boolean/nil values). Floats rejected with FunctionClauseError. Matches mppx/mpp-rs output for all MPP protocol data.
- `MPP.Verifier` — transport-neutral `verify/2` with the full verification pipeline: HMAC challenge binding, realm match, expiration, request match, method.verify. No Plug dependency.
- `MPP.Plug` refactored to a thin HTTP adapter delegating to `MPP.Verifier`.
- MCP `encode_request` updated from `Jason.encode!` to `JCS.canonicalize` (cross-SDK HMAC interop).

Verifier accepts keyword opts (`:secret_key`, `:realm`, `:method`, `:charge`, `:method_config`) rather than Plug types — zero coupling to HTTP transport. Always returns `{:ok, Receipt.t()} | {:error, Errors.t()}` with structured errors. JCS implemented inline (~30 lines) rather than adding a dependency. Dropped the `:request_serializer` option — JCS is mandatory per spec, not configurable.

Unblocked Tasks 32b (MCP server transport) and 33b (HTTP client transport).
task.implemented: Extracted the verification pipeline from MPP.Plug into a transport-neutral MPP.Verifier (verify/2 over keyword opts, returning {:ok, Receipt.t()} | {:error, Errors.t()}) and added MPP.JCS for RFC 8785 JSON canonicalization (MPP subset, floats rejected) — refactoring MPP.Plug into a thin HTTP adapter and switching MCP encode_request to JCS for cross-SDK HMAC interop.

task.body: Lift replay protection from Tempo-only to all payment methods. The `MPP.Tempo.Store` behaviour is already the right interface — reuse it at the Plug level.

task.title: Tempo SessionReceipt
task.body:
Added `MPP.Methods.Tempo.SessionReceipt` — session-intent receipt type paralleling `MPP.Receipt` (charge-intent).

- `new/1` sets method/intent/status defaults, auto-fills timestamp, defaults `reference` to `channel_id`.

Lesson that motivated this: a Tempo gas constant went stale (cold TIP-20 transfer cost drifted from ~272k to ~560k once Moderato added a protocol fee) and OOG-reverted on-chain, while the entire unit/stub suite stayed green. This class — wrong gas limit, wrong request shape, on-chain accounting drift — is structurally invisible to unit tests; only a live round-trip catches it. Integration must therefore run at a real cadence, not purely manually.

Separate the gate from the cadence: keep integration OUT of per-commit `precommit` (fails-closed in credential-less environments — CI, sibling repos, harness reviewer worktrees — and is non-deterministic/slow), and add a dedicated integration run that executes only where secrets live:

  * The same job as a required check on PR / merge to `main` and `development`.
  * Make missing credentials LOUD, never a silent green: when secrets are absent the integration suite must flunk with setup instructions (the exact env vars + how to obtain them), per the project's "never skip integration silently" rule — a 0-tests-ran "pass" is a lie.

task.body:
Make the Tempo `type="hash"` credential dedup commit atomic, matching both reference SDKs (mpp-rs `Store::put_if_absent`, mppx atomic `markHashUsed`). The atomic primitive already exists in `MPP.Methods.Tempo` (`reserve_hash_atomic`/store `check_and_mark`) and is used by the `type="transaction"` path; the hash path does not yet route its commit through it.

task.title: Presenter-identity binding for Tempo hash-credential path (close GHSA-34g7-vx6g-82mq residual)
acceptance_criteria: A third party who only observed a settled transfer cannot claim it against their own challenge on the hash/transaction paths (regression test proves the race is closed)

task.body:
Close the residual documented in the published advisory GHSA-34g7-vx6g-82mq. The 0.6.4 fix (static memo now requires a dedup store) closed unlimited passive replay, but on the `type="hash"` / `type="transaction"` Tempo paths the dedup key is the on-chain tx hash alone — nothing binds the credential *presenter* to the wallet that actually broadcast the transfer. With a store configured this leaves a front-running race: a party who observes a victim's settled transfer can submit that tx hash against their own fresh challenge and win if they get there first. The `type="proof"` path already binds presenter identity by verifying a signature from the paying wallet; extend an equivalent binding to the hash/transaction paths so the submitter must prove control of the transfer's sender address.

This is a deliberate hardening divergence: neither mpp-rs nor mppx requires presenter binding on the hash path today (verified: refs/mpp-rs/src/protocol/methods/tempo/method.rs `verify_hash` defaults the expected sender to the receipt's `from` with no presenter proof). So design for interoperability — do not break clients that legitimately present a hash for their own transfer. Prefer an opt-in server config (e.g. require a presenter signature only when configured) or a mechanism that a compliant client can satisfy, rather than a hard break. Cross-check the sender-recovery / signature-envelope layout against refs/mpp-rs + refs/mppx before pinning any wire detail (wire-format rule).

When this lands, update GHSA-34g7-vx6g-82mq to note the residual is fixed in the shipping version, and move docs/security-parity.md's row to a closed state.

Advertised as presenterBinding in 402 details. Off by default (SDK-divergent hardening). lib/mpp/methods/tempo.ex + tempo_test.exs (19 unit) + tempo_integration_test.exs (3 Moderato). 0.8.0.

Broad shared-helper extraction and MPP.Headers split (Task 73)
Making con_cache a genuinely optional dep — it is already a hard dep; only the stale 'optional' doc claim is corrected here
task.body:
Make on-chain replay protection secure-by-default, matching both reference SDKs. Public issue #7 (github.com/ZenHive/mpp/issues/7, reporter chenshj73) correctly flags that our on-chain dedup store defaults to nil → no-op, so a stateless default deployment can accept the same tx hash / credential repeatedly within the challenge window (repeated fulfillment for one payment). Both reference SDKs default an in-memory dedup store instead: mpp-rs `tempo()` builder sets `store: Some(Arc::new(MemoryStore::new()))` with an explicit `without_store()` opt-out (refs/mpp-rs/src/server/tempo.rs:186-187,127-131, test `tempo_builder_defaults_to_a_store`); mppx does `parameters.store ?? Store.memory()` for the non-zero charge/hash path (refs/mppx/src/tempo/server/Charge.ts:71-74). We are the outlier — flip the default.

Mechanism (con_cache is ALREADY a hard, non-optional dep at mix.exs:83, so this adds no dependency): wire the currently-stub `MPP.Application` — uncomment `mod: {MPP.Application, []}` in mix.exs:38 and start a default `MPP.Tempo.ConCacheStore` child in application.ex — then resolve an absent/nil on-chain method store (`method_config["store"]` for Tempo at tempo.ex and EVM at evm.ex) to that app-started default. Primary target is the per-method on-chain dedup store (that is what the SDKs default and what issue #7 is about); also evaluate whether the plug-level generic credential guard (`MPP.Plug` Config.store / replay_store/2, deliberately skipped for Tempo today) should default too — note that Tempo-skip interaction rather than break it.

The load-bearing API change: today `store: nil`/absent means "no-op" (the ONLY falsy value accepted by the three `validate_store!` copies in plug.ex:153, tempo.ex:292, evm.ex:378, and by replay_store/2 clause 1 at plug.ex:338). Introduce an explicit opt-out sentinel (e.g. `store: :none` or `false`, mirroring mpp-rs `without_store()`) that preserves today's stateless no-op, and free absent/nil to mean "use the default store." Route all three `validate_store!` copies + replay_store/2 through ONE shared resolution point in MPP.Tempo.Store so nil-vs-default-vs-opt-out is decided identically everywhere (do not re-hand-roll it three ways; the broader helper extraction stays Task 73).

Interactions to get right: (1) `validate_memo_store_binding!/1` (tempo.ex:321-331) currently raises on a static memo without a store — under the default it must resolve the EFFECTIVE store first: a static-memo config with no `store` key now SUCCEEDS (defaults), but static-memo + explicit opt-out sentinel must STILL raise (the operator affirmatively chose the unsafe stateless+static-memo combo). (2) Default ConCacheStore TTL must be ≥ challenge expires_in (Task 71 raises it to 600s = 2× the 300s default; depend on that). (3) Zero-amount/proof credentials: mpp-rs shares the same store for proof single-use (mpp:proof: namespace, method.rs:1581) while mppx leaves proof replay opt-in (Charge.ts:75-79, documented gap). Adopt mpp-rs behavior — the default store also makes proof credentials single-use — and document the choice. (4) Preserve the distinct key namespaces (mpp:charge: / mpp:evm: / mpp:proof:) so one default store instance backs all paths without collision.

Deployment caveat to document loudly (both SDKs carry near-identical language): the built-in default is an in-memory per-NODE store — it does NOT dedup across a horizontally-scaled cluster. Multi-instance operators must still pass a shared store (Redis/distributed). README + the Tempo/EVM/ConCacheStore moduledocs must state this.

This is a BREAKING default flip: every existing deployment that omits `:store` moves from stateless no-op to dedup-on. Ship it in a version bump (0.7.0) with a clear CHANGELOG breaking-change note and the one-line opt-out for anyone who genuinely wants stateless. The flip is toward safety; the only negatively-affected callers are those who deliberately wanted no state, and they get the opt-out sentinel.

Also correct the stale `con_cache` "optional dependency" doc claims (con_cache_store.ex:5, tempo.ex moduledoc) — it is a hard dep today; adjacent to Task 71's onchain/onchain_tempo doc fix but a separate module. On landing: respond to and close issue #7, and note that presenter-identity binding (Task 75) remains the separate front-running residual a default store does not close.

task.title: Release Tempo subscription activation claims after failed settlement
acceptance_criteria: A retryable activation settlement failure (broadcast/RPC error or reverted first-period transfer) does not permanently consume the activation credential

task.body:
Activation currently claims the Tempo dedup key before broadcast (`claim_activation/2` in `MPP.Methods.Tempo.Subscription`). Renewal already releases its in-flight claim on retryable failures (broadcast, simulate, revert) and keeps the claim when a confirmed transfer misses the recipient. Activation has no matching release: a reverted or RPC-failed first period burns `type="keyAuthorization"` so the client cannot retry. Evidence: `lib/mpp/methods/tempo/subscription.ex` `activate/4` claims then broadcasts; `test/mpp/methods/tempo/subscription_test.exs` covers reverted activation not persisting a record but does not assert the credential remains reusable.

Orchestrator decisions (resolved 2026-08-19):
- Release the claim ONLY on failures that prove non-inclusion: pre-broadcast validation/simulate rejections and confirmed reverts. On an ambiguous broadcast/transport error where the node may have included the tx, KEEP the claim held (fail-safe against double settlement) — same policy renewal follows.
- Gate release on `MPP.Tempo.Store.update_capable?/1` (v0.13.0). For stores that only implement `check_and_mark/2`, keep the claim held and surface a documented, actionable error telling the operator the store cannot release activation claims; do not invent a second claim mechanism.

Authority: live Moderato settlement plus the existing renewal claim policy in this module. Reference SDKs are compatibility evidence only.

Task 96 shipped durable Stripe subscription state, canonical-period renewal accounting, and cancel/2 — but two normative behaviors from draft-stripe-subscription-00 remain (run run-1787143475109-5e2b6677 review evidence):

1. Stripe-initiated cancellation: treat `customer.subscription.deleted` (and equivalent cancellation state) as revocation for future renewals. After webhook authenticity checks, mark the matching method-neutral subscription record so `process_invoice` rejects periods whose start is at or after the deletion — without deleting the record. 2. Stale invoice collection: if a renewal invoice is still unpaid when a later canonical period begins, drive the Stripe invoice to a non-collectible state (void / mark uncollectible / disable automatic collection) so a late Stripe retry cannot collect a closed period. Local `process_invoice` already rejects non-consecutive and already-charged periods; this task closes the Stripe-side hole.

task.body: An MCP server behind `MPP.Mcp.call/3` has to tell clients which payment methods and intents it accepts before they attempt a call, but MPP ships no helper for the `initialize` capability map — so every server hand-rolls it. `api_toolkit` currently maintains its own `ApiToolkit.MCP.Payment.capabilities/1` building `%{experimental: %{payment: %{methods: %{name => %{intents: [...]}}}}}`, and mppx/mpp-rs will each need the same. Owning it here also pins the shape cross-SDK instead of letting three implementations drift.

task.title: Fix: JSON-RPC adapter crashes on a non-map handler result
acceptance_criteria: A `:nested` call whose handler returns a non-map result (string, list, number) returns a well-formed JSON-RPC response instead of raising
Regression test covers `:nested` with each non-map result type, asserting no FunctionClauseError after a successful payment
Decide and document where the receipt goes when the result cannot carry `_meta` — envelope-level, or an explicit error
task.body:
`attach_response_receipt/4` has three clauses: an `"error"` passthrough, a `:nested` clause guarded by `is_map(result)`, and a `:root` clause. In `:nested` mode with a non-map result the guard fails and the third clause does not match `:nested`, so the call raises `FunctionClauseError` — *after* `Replay.mark_used/2` has already claimed the credential. The caller is charged and gets a crash.

`wrap_handler_response/2` explicitly accepts binary/list/number/boolean/nil results, so this shape is reachable through the documented handler contract. MCP `tools/call` results are always maps in practice, which is why it has not surfaced; the generic JSON-RPC transport makes it easier to hit.
